evals.name: membr-epochs
evals.prompt: Debrief commit HEAD of this repository (compare it with HEAD^): what changed, and why.
evals.expected_output: A one-line constant change whose value is in the numbers and the why. The page must not invent a reason the commit does not give.

questions.question: A model has a 1,000,000-token window. A turn ends with the epoch at 200k tokens. Does the next turn start in a new epoch? What was the answer before this commit?
questions.answer: Now: no, the limit is 220k. Before: yes, the limit was 150k.

questions.question: A model has a 200,000-token window. What is the epoch limit before and after this commit?
questions.answer: Before: 150k (min of 150k and 80% = 160k). After: 160k (80% of the window, as 220k > 160k).

questions.question: Below which window size does the 80% rule set the limit, before and after?
questions.answer: Before: 187,500 tokens. After: 275,000 tokens.

questions.question: The status shows the epoch after a 42k-token turn on a 1M window. What does it show now?
Why is there a limit below the window at all, and what happens when a turn goes over the window?
questions.answer: Past the limit each request costs more and the model reads its context less well. Over the window the turn fails with "Prompt is too long"; membr starts a new epoch, writes a note, and the user sends the message again.
must: past the limit requests cost more or the model reads its context less well
over the window the turn fails with "Prompt is too long"
the user sends the message again

questions.question: Does the commit say why it picked 220k?
questions.answer: No. A page that gives a reason must mark it as not from the commit.

evals.name: mobile-one-error
evals.prompt: Debrief commit HEAD of this repository (compare it with HEAD^): what changed, and why.
evals.expected_output: A UI change across 40 files: one owner and one presenter for a Host fault, before and after.

questions.question: A Host does not answer. The user is on the Host Screen. How many error rows and buttons show, before and after?
questions.answer: Before: two red rows (Listing and Topics), each with its own Retry. After: one row at the top of the tab with one Try again.
must: before: two error rows, each with its own Retry
after: one row with one Try again

questions.question: Which part of the app owns the Host Problem, and why there?
questions.answer: The Connections, one per Host, because every use of a Host goes through them.
must: every use of a Host goes through them

questions.question: The Host answers but refuses a read. Is that a Host Problem? Who shows it?
questions.answer: No. It stays a `failed` state with the Host's words, shown by the screen that asked.
must: the screen that asked shows it

questions.question: The Host Screen shows a Host Problem. Another use of the same Host then reaches it. What does the Host Screen do?
questions.answer: The Host Problem clears, and the Host Screen holds the Host again without a tap.
must: the Host Screen holds or reads the Host again with no tap

questions.question: Which label goes on the button for: a lost link, any other failed connect or read, a failed Host Write?
questions.answer: Reconnect; Try again; Retry.
must: Try again for other connects and reads

questions.question: In the Title Sheet, the user's last act failed and the Host also has a Host Problem. Which notice shows?
questions.answer: The act's error, because it answers the last tap. The Host Problem comes next, then a refused Topic read.
must: the error of the user's act

questions.question: A read fails on its Connection. When does that record a Host Problem?
questions.answer: When it fails on its Connection two times: the first failure makes the app read again.
must: on the second failure on its Connection

evals.name: muxify-pin
evals.prompt: Debrief commit HEAD of this repository (compare it with HEAD^): what changed, and why.
evals.expected_output: A state and ordering change: Pin for Board Sessions and the new Unpin rule.

questions.question: Can a Board Session be Pinned, before and after?
questions.answer: Before: no, only Topics. After: yes, as a Topic is.

questions.question: An In Play place is free. The user Unpins a Topic. Where does the card go, before and after?
questions.answer: Before: the top of the Bench, where a new Topic goes, so with a free In Play place it took that place. After: the end of the Guests, as a Guest; the Open Place stays open.
must: before: the top of the Bench
after: the end of the Guests, as a Guest

questions.question: Why does Unpin not fill the free In Play place?
questions.answer: The user wants the card where they can see it, and one rule for every card is easier to predict. The Bench holds only Topics, so a Board Session could not go there.
must: the card stays where the user can see it, or one rule for every card
a Board Session cannot go to the Bench

questions.question: A Board Session that is a Guest is Pinned. Where does it go, and what happens to its Guest mark?
questions.answer: Last among the Pinned cards; it loses the Guest mark.

questions.question: tmux restarts. What happens to a Pinned Board Session?
questions.answer: It stays Dormant among the Pinned cards, with Reopen and Start Fresh.

questions.question: Which actions stay Topic-only on a Pinned Board Session?
questions.answer: Settle, Forget, the Topic Note and Tags. Bench is not offered either, because a Pinned card is not In Play.

questions.question: The Session of a Pinned Board Session ends. What happens to its card?
questions.answer: The card leaves the Board and leaves no Open Place.

evals.name: membr-epochs-plan
evals.prompt:
Goal: Keep an epoch until it reaches 220k tokens, not 150k.
Plan how you would change this repository to reach the goal.
evals.expected_output: A plan for a one-constant change that shows today's limit rule and what the new number changes, and asks what the code does not settle.

questions.question: A model has a 1,000,000-token window. Today, at how many tokens does a turn start a new epoch, and what sets that number?
questions.answer: 150k: the constant EPOCH_BUDGET in packages/protocol; the limit is the smaller of it and 80% of the window.
must: the smaller of it and 80% of the window

questions.question: Where does the user see the 150k number today?
questions.answer: In the status line ("epoch 42k / 150k") and in the Settings popover's Epoch size; the docs (README, CONTEXT.md) also name it.

questions.question: What happens today when a turn goes over the model's window?
questions.answer: The turn fails with "Prompt is too long"; membr starts a new epoch, writes a note, and the user sends the message again.
must: the turn fails with "Prompt is too long"
the user sends the message again

decisions: Whether the 80%-of-window rule for small windows stays as it is
Whether the tests that use a 200k window change, because at 200k the limit becomes 160k and no longer shows 220k

evals.name: mobile-one-error-plan
evals.prompt:
Goal: When a Host cannot be reached, show one error with one Try again, not several.
Plan how you would change this repository to reach the goal.
evals.expected_output: A plan that shows why one fault shows several errors today, and asks where the fault should have one owner.

questions.question: A Host does not answer, and the user opens the Host Screen. What shows today?
questions.answer: Two red rows with the same text, one for the Listing and one for the Topics, each with its own Retry.

questions.question: Why does one fault show more than once today?
questions.answer: Each reader of the Host catches the same SSH failure and shows its own error, because no part owns the fault.
must: each reader shows its own error

questions.question: How many functions turn a connection failure into words today?
questions.answer: Two: one for the Attach and one for the screens.

decisions: Where the fault lives: one owner for the whole app, one per Host in the Connections, or a fix in the two screens only
Whether a refusal from a Host that answered counts as the same problem
The button labels: Reconnect, Try again and Retry, and when each applies

evals.name: muxify-pin-plan
evals.prompt:
Goal: Let me Pin a Board Session, and make Unpin put any card at the end of the Guests.
Plan how you would change this repository to reach the goal.
evals.expected_output: A plan that shows today's Pin and Unpin rules for Topics, and asks the choices that a Pinned Board Session opens.

questions.question: Can the user Pin a Board Session today?
questions.answer: No. Only a Topic can be Pinned; ADR 0102 says a Board Session is never Pinned.

questions.question: Where does Unpin put a Topic today?
questions.answer: At the top of the Bench, where a new Topic goes.

questions.question: Which actions work only on a Topic today, and not on a Board Session?
questions.answer: Bench, Settle, Forget, the Topic Note and Tags; a Board Session's card leaves the Board with Bench.

decisions: Where Unpin puts a card: the next free In Play place, or the end of the Guests
Which actions stay Topic-only on a Pinned Board Session
How the protocol carries the Pin of a Board Session: widen in place, or a new capability with a fallback
What a Pinned Board Session is after a tmux restart

evals.name: membr-epochs-debrief
evals.prompt: Commit HEAD of this repository carries out the planning page {asked}. Both of its decisions were answered with the recommended option. Debrief the commit against that plan.
evals.expected_output: A debrief that matches each asked item of the plan to the commit, with file:line, finds no difference and no unasked change, and says which tests ran.

questions.question: The plan asked whether the epoch budget stays a constant or becomes a setting in config.json. What did the commit do, and where?
questions.answer: It kept a constant: EPOCH_BUDGET in packages/protocol/src/index.ts went from 150_000 to 220_000. No config key and no protocol field were added.

questions.question: After the commit, what epoch limit does a model with a 200,000-token window get, and does that match the plan?
questions.answer: 160k: the limit is still min(220k, 80% of the window), as the plan recommended for D2; epochLimit() did not change. The README now says the 80% rule applies under 275,000 tokens.
must: it matches the plan: the 80% rule (epochLimit) is unchanged

questions.question: The e2e tests used a 200,000-token fake window. What did the commit do with them, and was that in the plan?
questions.answer: It moved their fake window to 1,000,000, so they expect 'epoch 42k / 220k (19%)' and '42,000 of 220,000 tokens'. The plan recommended exactly this, to keep the 80% path in context.test.ts.

questions.question: Did the commit change any file the plan did not list, or leave out a file it listed?
questions.answer: No. The commit changes the seven files the plan listed: protocol index.ts, web main.ts, context.test.ts, browser.e2e.ts, pty.e2e.ts, README.md and CONTEXT.md.
must: no difference: the changed files are the ones the plan listed
